idea: Shared treasuries are run by committees: a multisig needs a council, a token vote needs turnout, and both hand custody to a permanent class of approvers. Daykeeper replaces the approvers with a clock. One public NEAR treasury; every round the right to run it for a day is sold by continuous auction to the highest bidder. When the round ends, anyone can ring the bell and the contract mints two function-call access keys on its own account and hands them to the winner: one scoped to grant (one transfer, capped at a percentage of the pool fixed at launch) and one scoped to say (the keeper posts as the treasury). Neither key can attach NEAR, so neither can move the principal; every privileged method re-checks block_timestamp, so the keeper's power expires at the deadline without a scheduler or an admin. Identity is checked against env::signer_account_pk(), because the keeper's key lives on the treasury account. The pool only grows, one capped grant leaves per round, and the record of who held the seat and what they gave is public and permanent. Live on testnet at commons.dk-dave.testnet with 10 unit tests; the repository includes a CLI that a judge can run to bid, settle, speak, grant, and watch five different abuses refused by the chain.
